item.title: Ukraine strikes 'one of the largest oil refineries' in southern Russia ahead of Putin-Trump meeting in China
item.description: Ukraine's military says its strikes hit a key oil refinery in Russia's Krasnodar Krai region ahead of President Donald Trump's meeting with Vladimir Putin.
item.content:encoded:
Ukraine's military said it struck "one of the largest oil refineries in southern Russia" in the lead up to President Donald Trump's meeting Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Trump will meet one-on-one with Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, China, a U.S. official confirmed to Fox News on Wednesday.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said explosions "rocked" Russia's Krasnodar Krai region last night and into this morning as Ukrainian forces "carried out air strikes against the Ilsky and Afipsky oil refineries, two key fuel suppliers in southern Russia."

"Explosions and smoke were reported in the vicinity of the Ilsky Oil Refinery. Storage tanks were hit," it added. "The Ilsky Oil Refinery is one of the largest oil refineries in southern Russia, with an annual processing capacity of approximately 6.6 million tons of crude oil. Its products are used, among other purposes, to meet the fuel requirements of the aggressor state's armed forces."

UKRAINE RELEASES VIDEO SHOWING DAMAGE TO PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE FOLLOWING 'UNPRECEDENTED OPERATION' IN CRIMEA

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said an oil processing unit at the Afipsky Oil Refinery was damaged.

"Located in southern Russia, they provide some of the shortest supply routes for delivering fuel to Russian forces deployed on the frontline," it also said about the two facilities. "Consequently, every fire at these facilities means less diesel and petrol for the Russian military, and fewer oil revenues for the Russian aggressor to purchase missiles and Shahed-type attack drones."

TRUMP ARRIVES IN CHINA FOR HIGH-STAKES TRILATERAL TALKS WITH XI, PUTIN DURING IRAN WAR

The strikes unfolded as Russia launched drone attacks Wednesday on a residential area in Odesa, Ukraine, killing multiple people, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

"A brutal and deliberate strike directly against people, against life itself. And further proof of what the Russians really want and how they truly regard diplomatic efforts," Zelenskyy wrote on X.

"Without increasing global pressure on Russia, without real support for Ukraine, Russia will have no genuine reason to de-escalate and move toward peace," he added. "Those who want to negotiate peace do not escalate the killing."

Fox News' Lucas Tomlinson contributed to this report.

item.title: Man takes avoiding his baby momma to new heights as he climbs 30 to 40 feet up into a tree
item.description: A 32-year-old Tacoma man allegedly climbed 30 to 40 feet up a tree to avoid his baby momma, then jumped onto buses before being arrested.
item.content:encoded:
There's a new leader in the clubhouse when it comes to avoiding baby momma drama. He's a 32-year-old man who climbed into a tree last Tuesday night allegedly to avoid the mother of his child or children.

Deputies from the Pierce County Sheriff’s Office in Tacoma, Washington, responded to reports of a man stuck in a tree around 7:30 p.m. on Nov. 10 and found him "perched approximately 30 to 40 feet up in a tree."

The man would later claim that he had climbed the tree to avoid his "baby momma." That's a reasonable excuse in some cases. He had unfortunately picked a tree on a fenced property, which meant he wasn't passing go.

The sheriff's office reported that deputies watched as he "swung and bounced on the branches, raising concerns that he could fall and seriously injure himself" before he "jumped out of the tree and onto the top of a couple of buses parked below."

INFLUENCER AND HER LAWYER FATHER ARRESTED FOR ALLEGED MURDER-FOR-HIRE PLOT INVOLVING HER BABY DADDY

Those don't sound like the actions of a first timer. I don't know this for sure, but I have a feeling he's climbed a tree or two before to avoid his baby momma.

The deputies were able to convince him to climb down off the buses. That's where they say, "His adventure in the treetops came to an end."

The man was arrested for trespassing on the fenced property, and he was booked into the Pierce County Jail, according to the sheriff's office.

In the body cam footage, he can be heard explaining to the deputies how he ended up in the tree. He claimed that his baby momma had been following him and that he had a no-contact order against her.

The Pierce County Sheriff's Office didn’t address those claims in their Facebook post documenting the incident.

item.title: Protesters heckle Trump's ex-Border Patrol chief offstage after Dem governor condemns College Republican event
item.description: Protesters shouted "Immigrants are welcome here" as Gregory Bovino was escorted offstage at Rutgers College Republicans event Mikie Sherrill called "wrong."
item.content:encoded:
Protesters heckled former Trump Border Patrol commander-at-large Gregory Bovino off stage during a Monday night speech at Rutgers University, hours after New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill called the Rutgers College Republicans’ decision to host him "wrong" and urged the club to reconsider.

Bovino previously criticized Sherrill online, accusing her of prioritizing illegal immigrants over New Jersey residents. After returning to the stage, he called her "Sugar Pop Sherrill" and "Kim Jong Sherrill." Speaking to reporters afterward, he said she wanted to "trounce this freedom of speech," described the "Kim Jong Sherrill" label as "very fitting" and called the governor a "totalitarian." He also told Blaze News that Sherrill had timed her social media comments to "foment violence" against conservatives.

At Monday night’s Rutgers College Republicans event, protesters began shouting within minutes of Bovino taking the stage. Rutgers police escorted him offstage and ordered the hecklers to leave or face arrest, according to local reports. Bovino returned about ten minutes later to resume his remarks and answer questions. Hundreds of protesters also gathered outside.

30% OF COLLEGE STUDENTS SAY VIOLENCE ACCEPTABLE WAY TO STOP SPEAKERS ON CAMPUSES, SURVEY FINDS

"What’s so crazy is that you all allowed a Nazi to be here," a protester yelled as the heckling began. Another shouted, "Your fascist death cult is failing!" Video from inside the event captured chants of "Get out of New Jersey!" and "Immigrants are welcome here!" Outside, hundreds of protesters carried images of Renee Good and Alex Pretti, who were shot and killed by federal agents in Minneapolis.

Before Bovino’s Monday appearance, Rutgers told Fox News Digital it was committed to protecting freedom of expression and maintaining campus security. The university also said hosting a student-organized event did not constitute an endorsement of the speaker or his views. Rutgers had not responded to Fox News Digital's follow-up request for comment about the disruption by publication.

Hours before Bovino’s speech, Sherrill said in a social media post that she was "deeply disappointed" by the Rutgers College Republicans’ invitation, adding, "Giving him a platform is the wrong decision."

Sherrill said that if the club went ahead with the event, she would ensure the state worked with Rutgers to protect "the safety of everyone and the rights enshrined in our Constitution," and she urged attendees to question Bovino about his record.

SHERRILL COMMITS $20.2M TO DEPORTATION DEFENSE WHILE CONDEMNING RUTGERS OVER BORDER PATROL SPEAKER

Fox News Digital contacted Sherrill's team for comment on the disruption at Bovino’s event but received no response before publication.

Bovino served as Trump's commander-at-large of the U.S. Border Patrol and oversaw immigration enforcement and deportation operations, including Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis. He was removed from command in January following the shootings of Good and Pretti and retired from the Border Patrol in March.

During the Rutgers College Republicans event, a student asked Bovino about the deaths of Good and Pretti. He replied, "Poor decisions come with consequences," then said the circumstances were "still being sorted out." Bovino called ICE agents the "real victims" and added, "I love them and salute them."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Asked after Monday’s event whether he stood by the deaths of Pretti and Good, Bovino said, "I didn’t stand by anybody’s death."

He clarified that his earlier comment about going "harder" referred to mass deportation operations, not the shootings of Good or Pretti. Bovino said he would rejoin the Border Patrol "in an instant" to continue those operations and called the end of enforcement activity in Minnesota "the great surrender." He added that he hoped the administration would complete its mass deportation efforts but feared it would "surrender" its aggressive deportation agenda.

item.title: Russell Brand could be banned from contacting wife after 'appalling' prison message
item.description: Russell Brand's prison message read by wife Laura Brand is being urgently investigated, and he could face a communication ban under the Prison Rules 1999.
item.content:encoded:
Russell Brand could face serious consequences — including being banned from communicating with his wife, Laura Brand — after releasing an "appalling" message from behind prison bars.

According to the regulations governing prisons in England and Wales, authorities can restrict a prisoner's contact with the outside world.  Brand — who was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault — could face such restrictions if found to have violated rules governing outside communications.

On Sunday, Brand claimed he is "not guilty" in a message read by Laura during an episode of the couple's weekly Sunday Service YouTube vlog.

RUSSELL BRAND’S WIFE DEFENDS ACTOR AT RAPE TRIAL WHILE ADMITTING HIS PAST MONOGAMY STRUGGLES

Shortly after the message was shared publicly, a spokesperson for British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in a statement to Deadline: "This is clearly appalling and is being urgently investigated. We expect action to be taken if he’s found to have broken the rules."

"Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims, and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances. Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments."

BEAR GRYLLS ADDRESSES RUSSELL BRAND'S BAPTISM, CALLS VICTIMS 'HEROES OF THE DAY' AFTER VERDICT

On Monday, Lord Chancellor and Secretary of State Alex Norris wrote on X: "The broadcast of a statement from Russell Brand is completely unacceptable. Prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims."

"This is being urgently investigated, and I expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules."

RUSSELL BRAND SPARKS PRISON INVESTIGATION AFTER WIFE READS DEFIANT MESSAGE FOLLOWING RAPE CONVICTION

Trial attorney and former prosecutor Imran Ansari questioned the backlash to Brand’s message during an appearance on the "Crime & Justice with Donna Rotunno" podcast, arguing that the statement asserted innocence without targeting his accusers.

"They’re declaring that innocence without necessarily attacking anyone. They don’t bring up a woman at all," Ansari said.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Asked about the potential consequences, Ansari suggested Brand could face restrictions on communications with reporters or other media figures, but acknowledged he did not know what action, if any, prison officials would take.

"It’s typical that a prisoner who maintains their innocence will release statements," he said. "I don’t know what Russell Brand now will face because of this."

RUSSELL BRAND’S WIFE OPENS UP AFTER COMEDIAN’S RAPE CONVICTION, SHARES MESSAGE FROM IMPRISONED HUSBAND

In the message, Brand claimed his innocence while confirming he is currently being jailed at HMP Littlehey, a prison for individuals who have been convicted of sexual offenses.

"Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening," Laura read from a notebook.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"The good news is that Christ is with us when we choose him, and I do. I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey. Little as in small, and hey as in, ‘Hey, I’m in the biggest sex offenders’ prison in Europe. The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated," she continued. "And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone."

"I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me. Let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us."

"Please support my treasured wife and family. I feel your prayers, your brother in Christ. Russell," she concluded the note.

Brand was sentenced on Nov. 9.

RUSSELL BRAND FOUND GUILTY OF ONE COUNT OF RAPE AND THREE COUNTS OF SEXUAL ASSAULT

Brand has denied the charges and was acquitted of two additional rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.

He was immediately taken into custody following the verdict, according to the BBC.

Brand was accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009.

item.title: The Rock says he will appear at WWE's Survivor Series: WarGames as company celebrates his career
item.description: The Rock says he pushed back the "Jumanji" movie tour by a week so he could appear at WWE Survivor Series: WarGames in Houston next weekend.
item.content:encoded:
WWE is celebrating 30 years of The Rock – one of the most electrifying men to ever enter the sports entertainment realm – and with that, he said Wednesday he’s set to appear at the next premium live event.

The Rock appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" as he gets set for an appearance on "College GameDay" later this week on the campus of the University of Miami. He was asked whether he would appear in WWE again. The Rock had a surprising response.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

"Here’s the truth. I would not miss next week for the world, man," he said. "I’m going to Houston. Houston, we don’t have a problem. I’m going to Houston. I’m gonna go to Survivor Series."

Survivor Series: WarGames is one of the big four premium live events on the WWE calendar. It’s the crescendo to end the year and the event that will reset everything ahead of the Royal Rumble as pro wrestling fans start to get excited for WrestleMania season.

The Rock said he moved his movie tour schedule around to make time for Survivor Series: WarGames. His first match came at Survivor Series in 1996 and was the sole survivor of the classic 5-on-5 elimination tag team match. He was known as Rocky Maivia at that time but the moment helped set the stage for what The Rock would become in pro wrestling.

"As a matter of fact, I actually said, as you know, we start our big ‘Jumanji’ tour next weekend, I actually talked with Sony about three months ago and pushed the tour a couple of days – actually by a week – so I can make this event. And I can’t wait. And, honestly, man, everything you said from Rocky Maivia, ‘People’s Champ,’ ‘Corporate Champ,’ ‘Final Boss,’ ‘Nation of Domination,’ which is all the iterations of this character.

"It was always so close to my heart, still is because it’s deep in my bones, it doesn’t happen without the people. You hear that often, but it’s true. That moniker of ‘People’s Champion’ that Muhammad Ali granted me back in the day, that means something to me. So, ‘People’s Champ’ is coming home.

"I’ll see everybody next week at Survivor Series."

There are a ton of questions that will loom as The Rock returns. He hasn’t been seen since Elimination Chamber 2025 when he ushered in John Cena’s heel turn, which Cena himself has said didn’t go the way he wanted.

The big match that many who have watched WWE have hoped for is The Rock going up against world heavyweight champion Roman Reigns. It would be a part of a longer Bloodline storyline that dates back to when The Rock inserted himself into WrestleMania 40, developing a feud with Cody Rhodes. WrestleMania 40 was The Rock’s last actual match in WWE.

For what it’s worth, The Bloodline will take on 946 in a WarGames match at Survivor Series next weekend.

item.title: Senate Republicans advance Trump's effort to abolish Dept of Education
item.description: Senate Republicans, led by Jim Banks, push a 10-bill package to permanently transfer Department of Education programs, codifying Trump's dismantling order.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Senate Republicans are advancing a major legislative push to dismantle the Department of Education, introducing a 10-bill package aimed at permanently transferring the agency’s core programs to other federal departments.

Sen. Jim Banks, R-Ind., introduced the Senate companion to the Less Bureaucracy, Better Education legislative package on Wednesday, which would codify President Donald Trump and Education Secretary Linda McMahon’s executive actions to wind down the department. Sens. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., and Ashley Moody, R-Fla., are co-sponsoring the Senate effort.

"The federal education bureaucracy has failed students and families for decades. President Trump and Secretary McMahon are finally putting parents first and returning power where it belongs. Our bills will make their reforms permanent, eliminate layers of Washington bureaucracy and ensure taxpayers are no longer forced to prop up a failed department," Banks told Fox News Digital.

DEPT OF ED PUSHES AHEAD WITH EFFORTS TO DISMANTLE FEDERAL BUREAUCRACY AFTER BLUE WAVE

Throughout his 2024 presidential campaign, Trump promised to eliminate the Department of Education, later signing a March 2025 executive order directing McMahon to begin dismantling the 45-year-old agency. While fully abolishing a Cabinet-level department requires congressional approval — and 60 votes to overcome a Senate filibuster — Republicans are moving to lock in the administration's restructuring piece by piece.

McMahon told Fox News Digital that the department acts primarily as a pass-through entity for federal dollars and contends that its day-to-day operations are nonessential.

"For too long, an overgrown Washington bureaucracy has funneled trillions of taxpayer dollars into top-down mandates and administrative red tape. Exactly one year after we announced six critical partnerships to begin reversing that trend, Senators Banks, Tuberville, Moody and Lee are introducing the ‘Less Bureaucracy, Better Education’ package to permanently codify the Trump Administration’s historic reforms," she said.

She went on to say, "This vital legislation will make permanent the work we have done to align programs with the agencies best suited to support them and return education authority to those closest to the child. I commend their leadership in launching this important effort, and I look forward to working together to improve education for our students and families." 

The Senate introduction follows 10 interagency agreements signed between May 2025 and March 2026 across five federal departments — Labor, Treasury, Health and Human Services, State and Interior — as the Education Department seeks to shrink its footprint.

TRUMP’S FIRST-YEAR GOVERNMENT OVERHAUL DELIVERS CHANGE WASHINGTON HASN’T SEEN SINCE THE 1960S

For example, the Department of Labor took on a major role in the day-to-day administration of adult education, family literacy and career and technical education programs under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Perkins Act. While Labor manages operational duties, the Department of Education retains statutory oversight as services shift to states and grant recipients.

In another major move, the agency partnered with the Department of the Treasury to assume operational responsibility for managing the federal student loan portfolio and collecting on defaulted student debt.

MCMAHON CALLS FOR 'RESET' OF EDUCATION AFTER US SPENT $3 TRILLION AND STILL SAW READING SCORES DECLINE

According to Department of Education officials, the goal of the partnerships is to demonstrate a "proof of concept" to Congress that essential federal education functions and funding flows can be reallocated across executive branch agencies without disruption. An agency official previously told Fox News Digital that staffers are effectively working to put themselves out of a job under Trump's orders because the department is unnecessary.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS ‘HARD RESET’ FOR AMERICAN SCHOOLS, VOWS TO PUT PARENTS ‘BACK IN CHARGE’

The House Education and Workforce Committee, led by Chairman Tim Walberg, R-Mich., already advanced its version of the 10-bill package along party lines in July.

"Every student deserves an education that works for them, yet the status quo is failing our children. Republicans believe in a new vision that puts students, families and educators in the driver’s seat. I am glad to see my colleagues in the Senate take action to end the bureaucracy and deliver on that vision for the American people," Walberg told Fox News Digital.

CHARTER SCHOOL FOUNDER BACKS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PUSH TO DECENTRALIZE K-12 EDUCATION

Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, echoed that sentiment, arguing that Washington has sidelined local communities for too long.

"For too long, the centralized bureaucracy of the Department of Education has overridden state and local control of schooling while failing America’s families. As President Trump returns education to the people, our legislation returns the remaining worthwhile function of the Department to other appropriate federal agencies," Lee told Fox News Digital.

The Education Department announced earlier this year it moved to a smaller building to reduce the agency's footprint as part of its broader effort to dismantle itself.

Department staff will move out of the Lyndon B. Johnson headquarters building, so the Department of Energy can eventually move in by August.

"Our schools are supposed to be preparing the next generation of Americans for LIFE — not pushing some woke ideology. I’m proud to introduce this bill with Sen. Banks to codify one of President Trump’s biggest promises — dismantling the [ED]. Let’s put our students first and get it done," Sen. Tuberville told Fox News Digital.

item.title: 16 Ecuadorian fishermen sue US government, allege drone attack destroyed their boat near the Galápagos
item.description: Ecuadorian fishermen allege U.S. drones struck their boat in the Pacific Ocean near the Galápagos, forcing the crew to jump overboard, a lawsuit says.
item.content:encoded:
More than a dozen Ecuadorian fishermen have sued the federal government, alleging they were wrongly targeted in a drone strike that destroyed their boat in the Pacific Ocean earlier this year as part of the Trump administration’s broader campaign against vessels suspected of drug trafficking.

The 16 fishermen aboard La Negra Francisca Duarte II say drones launched from a U.S. vessel struck their boat March 17, 2026, as they headed home from a two-week fishing trip near the Galápagos.

The strike set the boat ablaze, forcing the crew to jump overboard and escape in lifeboats, according to a lawsuit filed Monday in federal court in Pennsylvania. All 16 survived, but two suffered serious burns. One man’s leg was burned to the bone, the lawsuit says.

The fishermen’s lawyers say the crew had no ties to drug cartels or terrorist groups and posed no imminent threat when U.S. drones struck their vessel, which they say had been cleared by Ecuadorian authorities hours earlier.

US MILITARY LAUNCHES FIRST AUTONOMOUS WARFARE COMMAND TO DEPLOY UNMANNED SYSTEMS ACROSS LATIN AMERICA

After their boat was destroyed, the fishermen sailed toward a blue vessel, which the lawsuit identified as a U.S. ship. Some personnel wore U.S. Coast Guard vests, the suit says. They allegedly zip-tied the uninjured men, hooded them and forced them to stand barefoot on the hot metal deck with no food and little water.

One injured fisherman was taken below deck for treatment, where U.S. personnel allegedly told him they had carried out the drone strike and laughed about destroying the boat, according to the lawsuit.

The fishermen were held until the next day before they were put on an El Salvadoran ship that took them back to El Salvador, where they were held at a migrant center in "deplorable conditions" until the end of March.

THE UNLIKELY SOUTH AMERICAN ALLY HELPING LEAD TRUMP'S DRUG CARTEL CRACKDOWN

The Department of War and the U.S. Coast Guard have denied knowing about or being involved in the March 17 attack on La Negra Francisca Duarte II.

U.S. Southern Command declined to comment, citing its policy of not issuing statements on pending or ongoing litigation.

The lawsuit argues that the Trump administration’s strikes in the Caribbean and Pacific violate federal and international law because they have been carried out outside an armed conflict. It adds that even if an armed conflict existed, the attacks could constitute war crimes under the Geneva Conventions.

The plaintiffs are seeking compensatory and other financial damages to be determined at trial, plus an injunction ordering the U.S. to end similar boat attacks.

item.title: CodePink co-founder's $55M foundation reinstated in California amid grant questions
item.description: Medea Benjamin's Arc of Justice foundation regained California charitable registration after missed filings, but it stays on probation through Aug. 2029.
item.content:encoded:
CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin’s $54.6 million family foundation has been reinstated as a California charity after years of missed financial filings, although questions linger over $2.7 million in grants it reported paying in 2024, the year its registration was suspended.

The foundation, Arc of Justice, has poured $24.6 million into protest groups, legal advocacy organizations and progressive nonprofits over more than two decades, a previous Fox News Digital investigation found. The 2024 payouts included $350,000 to CodePink, according to the foundation’s 2024 federal tax return.

Years of missed filings prompted regulators in California to revoke the foundation's charitable registration in January 2025 after more than a year of suspension for repeatedly failing to submit required annual reports or respond to regulatory notices.

State regulators restored it in September, placing the foundation on three years' probation.

$54M CODEPINK-LINKED FOUNDATION SHUT DOWN IN CALIFORNIA POPS UP AT RAMSHACKLE MIAMI HOME

Under California regulations, organizations with suspended or revoked charitable registrations are prohibited from distributing or spending charitable assets without the attorney general’s prior written approval, according to Title 11, Section 345(b) of to the California Code of Regulations.

Fox News Digital asked the California Attorney General’s Office whether the foundation needed or received approval to distribute those grants.

"While the organization was suspended from activity in California, our office received no information regarding the organization’s out-of-state activities," the office said.

The office added that "a California registration revocation does not apply to grants outside California by a foreign nonprofit doing business in other states."

Arc of Justice is a California-incorporated nonprofit and its charitable registration was suspended during 2024, before being revoked in January 2025.

The Attorney General’s Office did not directly address whether the foundation’s grants required or received written approval.

The foundation’s attorney, David Levitt, also did not answer Fox News Digital’s questions about whether the foundation obtained approval for the payments.

Regulators approved its reinstatement petition Sept. 9 after it submitted five years of overdue reports covering 2020 through 2024 and paid $1,800 in fees and penalties, according to the petition and state records.

Levitt previously said that foundation leaders mistakenly believed a planned relocation to Florida had ended its California reporting obligations.

"The Foundation's failure to comply with the Registry's registration and reporting requirements resulted from an administrative misunderstanding concerning the Foundation's state of registration," Levitt wrote in its reinstatement petition.

Fox News Digital previously reported that a new Florida nonprofit using the Arc of Justice name had been incorporated at the Miami home of Benjamin’s longtime partner, Tighe Barry, after California revoked the foundation’s charitable registration.

Levitt previously said the Florida corporation was created as a "placeholder" while the foundation considered relocating. He said the move was never completed, the California corporation was never formally dissolved and no assets were transferred.

LAWMAKERS RAISE ALARM OVER NEVILLE ROY SINGHAM'S $278M NETWORK SPREADING CCP PROPAGANDA IN THE U.S.

item.title: F1 legend Riccardo Patrese talks about F1's first failed attempt at racing in Las Vegas: 'It was a car park'
item.description: F1 great Riccardo Patrese recalls the forgotten Caesars Palace Grand Prix, when Formula 1 raced in a Las Vegas casino parking lot in the early '80s.
item.content:encoded:
Formula 1 is headed to the Las Vegas Strip this weekend for the fourth edition of the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

However, people sometimes forget that this is F1's second attempt at getting a race going in Sin City. Back in the early '80s, the series held the Caesars Palace Grand Prix.

It wasn't a race that is fondly remembered in the sport's history, and F1 great Riccardo Patrese pointed out one of the big reasons why.

F1 GREAT RICCARDO PATRESE EXPLAINS WHY HE TOLD KIMI ANTONELLI HE HAD TO WIN A CHAMPIONSHIP THIS SEASON

"That was a car park when I raced there," Patrese said over Zoom to promote Jackpot City Casino.

He's not kidding. The circuit really was set up in the hotel and casino's parking lot. And not exactly in a way that makes you forget it's a parking lot, as the Miami International Autodrome does.

"We came to Las Vegas, and it was a new Grand Prix, and coming to Vegas is always an interesting place to go, especially if it's the first time," Patrese said. "Let's say that it was strange because it was in a car park! But we raced in many strange places in those days. Bernie [Ecclestone, former F1 boss] wanted to have Formula One all around the world, and every opportunity that arose, he took it. So we came to Vegas with a lot of enthusiasm, and in the end, we did the Grand Prix."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The race was held twice, with Alan Jones winning for Williams in 1981 and Michele Alboreto winning for Tyrrell in 1982.

After that, F1 dropped it, but the circuit hosted both CART Indy Car and the Trans-Am Series in 1983 and 1984.

During Patrese's lengthy career in F1, which ran from 1977 to 1993, the series raced all over the United States.

"I liked Long Beach very much," Patrese said. "I nearly won the Grand Prix, but coming to the States was always nice. Every time that we came to the States and raced, we liked [it]. It's not that we didn't want to come, even in funny places."

Patrese pointed out Phoenix as an unusual race where teams dealt with intense heat, but also noted an affinity for another classic American circuit, Watkins Glen.

"Of course, Watkins Glen has also a big tradition," he said. "I raced [there] in Formula One, but even in [endurance racing] with Lancia. So, anyway, we came always with a lot of enthusiasm to the States for racing."

That enthusiasm is still there, as the Las Vegas Grand Prix is the last of three annual US races on the F1 calendar.

Although if they want to add Watkins Glen back to the schedule, you won't hear any complaints from me.

item.title: AI data centers could consume more water than Americans drink in a year by 2030, says CEO working on solution
item.description: Ecolab CEO Christophe Beck says AI data centers could drink as much water as Americans by 2030 unless direct chip cooling and water recycling catch on.
item.content:encoded:
Ecolab CEO Christophe Beck, whose company is working on sustainable solutions to ecological problems like AI data centers’ robust water consumption, said that without reform, AI data centers could wind up consuming more water than Americans drink every year.

"Ninety-five percent of the data centers today use a lot of water," he told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview. "We estimate that by 2030, with the old technologies in the U.S., we will use as much water to cool data centers as Americans are using for drinking needs."

DAVID MARCUS: WHAT BIG TECH’S WEEKEND FROM HELL MEANS FOR THE FUTURE OF DATA CENTERS

Beck argued that this phenomenon is "not sustainable," and laid out the technologies his company is working on in an effort to reduce data centers’ water consumption.

"Behind AI there's water in every step of the process. You need water to produce the chips, to power the chips and to cool the chips. And for the last four or five years, the chips generation that we were using were just cooled with air," he told Fox News Digital.

However, with the increasing complexity of chips to match an ever-building demand for computer power, air conditioning alone is no longer sufficient to cool chips in data centers, Beck explained.

"You need something that's way stronger. Water is 30 times better at extracting heat than air from the chips. So that's why many of those new data centers are moving toward direct chip water cooling, which ultimately is bringing cold water on top of the chip," he said.

Direct water cooling, he explained, has the dual benefits of increasing efficiency and sustainability, because the water used to cool the chips can be recycled and used on every chip in a given data center.

"So you end up in a place where you have a data center that is much more powerful [than] using no water, using less power, and ultimately not having an impact on natural resources and in communities around us, which is one of the unlocks that people are pushing back so much against right now," he said.

ONE INDUSTRY FACES MULTI-TRILLION-DOLLAR RECKONING AFTER HISTORIC MIDTERM ELECTION RESHUFFLE

On Nov. 4, voters across the U.S. elected lawmakers and executives who ran on campaigns to limit the number of data centers.

In Texas, Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa upset incumbent Republican Greg Abbott. Voters who ticked the box for Hinojosa did so after she campaigned heavily on instituting a data center moratorium, a fact that Beck took note of.

THE POWERFUL WAY AMERICAN COMMUNITIES CAN BENEFIT FROM THE NEW TECH BOOM REVEALED BY DATA CENTER CEO

"Most of the data centers that were installed in Texas or anywhere else in the country or in the world, for that matter, were using a lot of water, a lot of power. And that's created a lot of backlash from the communities, which is rightfully so," Beck told Fox News Digital.

Beck noted that while Texas is one of the most economically strong states in the union, it is also one of the most water-stressed.

"It's a bad combination," he said. "Obviously, high growth, great news; no water, less good news. So we've looked at those technological solutions on how do you bring higher growth, more data processing while using much less water."

Beck added that the technologies Ecolab is developing will exclusively be used in new-build data centers, while the political pushback is surrounding the existing, more resource-demanding projects.

Direct cooling allows for what is known as a closed loop system, a method that is far more sustainable and requires less water than previous iterations of water-cooling methods.

Ecolab, Beck explained, has found a way to recycle water not only in the chip cooling process, but in chip fabrication as well, a process that necessitates extremely pure water.

"The so-called fabs, they use huge amounts of water, which is very specialized water because it needs to be ultra pure," Beck explained.

"And that, to be recycled, is even way harder than in a data center. But even there, at Ecolab we found solutions to not only get the highest purity of water to get the most advanced chips, but we can reuse that water as well in ways that are water neutral," he said.

Beck also put in context just how pure the water for chip fabrication needs to be.

"The purity is a million times more pure than what you would inject in your blood if it's a drug. So super high quality, super high purity of water at the end," he said.

"So the way we do it, in short, is ultimately at every step of the process we try to extract the water from that process step. We treat, we purify that water, we bring it back to an ultra-pure water level, and we bring back to the process. And the very special thing that we have at Ecolab, within that water you have some trace materials that we call connected water," he said.

"So we understand the quality of the water throughout the process within the fab or the data center, for that matter, that we know exactly the quality of that water to make sure that the chips are perfectly produced. And we know what we need to do in order to re-treat that water so that it can be reused afterwards. And you end up with better chips, lower cost, and most importantly, water neutral," Beck said.

item.title: Best hikes in and around Morgantown ahead of West Virginia's Big 12 showdown with Houston
item.description: Morgantown hiking glows in November, from Raven Rock Trail's Cheat River Canyon views at Coopers Rock State Forest to Valley Falls State Park's waterfalls.
item.content:encoded:
The college football regular season may be winding down, but hiking season is in full swing.

Late autumn across America is a perfect time of year to get some of the most picturesque hikes in, as you take in all the crisp weather and fall foliage.

Today on the dockett is none other than God's Country: Almost heaven, West Virginia.

BEST HIKING SPOTS IN EUGENE, OREGON, AHEAD OF THE DUCKS' SHOWDOWN WITH THE MICHIGAN WOLVERINES

The Mountaineers are welcoming top-20 Houston to campus, which means Morgantown is our pick for this week's hiking spotlight.

I can't think of a better place for a November hike than northern West Virginia, which offers a nice mix of rugged Appalachian trails and wooded biomes that run along beautiful river gorges.

AMERICA'S BEST NATIONAL PARKS FOR FALL REVEALED — PLUS THE NPS DIRECTOR'S PERSONAL PICKS

Picking just a handful of spots was a tall task, as I could have realistically given you a couple dozen, but these are the cream of the crop.

If you make it to one hiking spot in Morgantown, make sure it's this one.

Coopers Rock offers some of the most breathtaking views in the entire Appalachian region, and that's saying a lot.

The entire forest has over 50 miles of trails, but the gem of them all is the Raven Rock Trail, which offers a winding path that leads to a view of Cheat River Canyon that will certainly be Instagram worthy.

This place has hikes for both beginners and advanced hikers, which is why it's the best bang-for-your-buck pick, along with the views that my words will never do justice.

It's a 20-minute drive from downtown Morgantown, so it won't be something that will tank an entire day, and you'll still have time to make it back to campus to reward yourself with a cheat meal at the end of a long hike.

If you're looking to get a solid hike in and want to experience the natural beauty of West Virginia without going vertical, check out Deckers Creek.

This trail has over 19 miles of hikable paths, and its main trailhead starts in downtown Morgantown, so you won't even have to find your car keys.

It's a terrific option for hikers who want to stay local and not kill their quads before game day, giving you a long walk with beautiful natural scenery to boot.

The former railroad corridor (where the trail gets its name) gives you plenty of paths through wooded valleys, wetlands, rocky outcroppings and several waterfalls.

Make sure you check out Deckers Creek Gorge, especially if you want a little bit more of a rugged walk with dramatic scenery.

Deckers Creek Rail Trail is where convenience meets beauty, so give it a try before you leave town.

Here's where things get a little easier while still offering all that everyone loves about West Virginia.

With approximately three miles of trails all located within West Virginia University's campus limits, Core Arboretum is the easy, relaxing option for beginners looking for a quick afternoon stroll through some of the finest natural beauty Morgantown has to offer.

This 91-acre natural escape is right in the heart of town and features more than 150 species of native plants nestled into botanical gardens and wooded ravines.

No, it's not the mountainous climb of Coopers Rock or the riverside romp of Deckers Creek, but the serenity you will experience at Core Arboretum will put your mind at ease even before or after the most stressful of college football games.

It's the most convenient option for visitors looking to take in the natural side of Morgantown without ever having to leave campus.

You know I have to do it every week, but if you're willing to take a bit of a drive and go on an adventure to find your thrills, Valley Falls State Park is the move.

It's about 30-40 minutes from campus, in nearby Fairmont, WV, but the drive is well worth it.

The waterfalls alone are worth the price of a tank of gas, and the fall foliage accenting the cascading falls will be something you'll never forget (and makes for a hell of an Instagram post).

Valley Falls has everything a seasoned hiker could ask for: rugged terrain, wooded trails, and scenic views.

It's roughly 1,200 acres of some of the best natural trails in the region.

Beginners shouldn't be intimidated either, as there are plenty of paths that offer a more forgiving route to the scenery.

This state park has something for everyone, and November might be the perfect time to go and appreciate some of the best West Virginia has to offer.

item.title: Recent service outages not state-sponsored attacks, DNI Jay Clayton testifies
item.description: DNI Jay Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee recent U.S. service outages stem from maintenance, not a coordinated state-sponsored attack.
item.content:encoded:
Recent service outages across U.S. systems stem from routine technical and maintenance issues – not a coordinated foreign cyberattack, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton testified Wednesday, even as he warned lawmakers that "superintelligence" is rapidly escalating the speed and sophistication of future cyber threats.

"Based on what we know today, after a great deal of digital diligence, these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes, " Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee's "Worldwide Threats to the Homeland: 25 Years After 9/11" hearing. "They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack."

Clayton acknowledged public concern over the timing of the recent outages, telling the panel that the American people are right to ask questions, but intelligence reviews point away from foreign interference.

THE OUTAGES AMERICA HAS SUFFERED WEREN'T AN ATTACK, BUT THE NEXT FAILURE COULD BE

"We have no indication that these events are related," Clayton said in response to persistent questioning from Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y. "But let me answer something that the American people should know, which is the speed of compute and the level of capability of applications that use that compute is increasing substantially, which means legacy systems that were old six months ago or a year are a lot older."

The intelligence community remains on alert and continues to monitor for any malicious cyber activity targeting U.S. networks or law enforcement partners, Clayton said in his opening statement.

"After doing a great deal of due diligence inside the government with the private sector, with people in the private sector whose job is cybersecurity, we have no indication that these incidents are related, that they're coordinated," Clayton reiterated in the question and answer session of the hearing. "We also have no indication that they're a result of a state-sponsored malign actor."

TIMELINE: AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS

Beyond the immediate outages, the intelligence chief warned lawmakers that rapid advancements in artificial intelligence – also referred to as "superintelligence" – are fundamentally altering the digital battlefield and raising the stakes for homeland defense.

"Let me note that superintelligence is reshaping the cybersecurity landscape, " Clayton said. "It is sharply increasing speed, scale, and sophistication of offensive and defensive cyber operations. And it's not just cyber. This goes to national security. It goes to the battlefield and it goes to commerce. Superintelligence is changing the way we do business, the way we fight wars and the way we combat terrorism every day."

GOVERNMENT INVESTIGATORS FIND AI PLATFORMS PRODUCE TERROR PLOT PLANS IN UNDERCOVER OP

During his opening remarks, Clayton outlined a broader heightened threat environment 25 years after the Sept. 11 attacks. While declining to discuss classified intelligence in an open setting, he noted that full briefings have been provided to the Gang of Eight and congressional intelligence committees.

Among the primary threats highlighted in his testimony:

Surveillance authorities: Clayton urged Congress not to let Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) expire, calling it the "single most indispensable tool" for early warnings on foreign threats to the homeland and U.S. troops.

"No other program can replicate the speed and effectiveness of FISA 702," Clayton said. "Letting it expire would simply be a mistake."

All 16 of Fears' points came from the free-throw line. He went 16-for-18 from the charity stripe while going 0-for-3 from the floor.

When it was all said and done, Michigan State's five starters went 1-for-28 from the floor, with the lone made bucket coming courtesy of Coen Carr from three-point land.

The Volunteers have built their brand during the Rick Barnes era around defensive effort, but nine made shots isn't just a result of defenders playing lights out; Michigan State's shooters were colder than cold.

Entering Tuesday's game, Michigan State was averaging 93 points per game, which included a 79-point outing against Duke. Scoring 47 points below your season average would fall under the category of anomaly.

item.title: US warns Americans in key locations to 'keep a low profile' ahead of crowded holiday travel
item.description: U.S. embassies in London, Berlin and Madrid issued holiday security alerts to traveling Americans, urging people to stay vigilant at festivals, markets and transit hubs.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. officials are warning Americans in certain locations to stay safe as the holiday season begins amid ongoing security concerns across the United Kingdom. 

A recent travel advisory was released by several U.S. embassies across Europe — including in London, Berlin and Madrid — on Monday, with Rome issuing a similar notice on Wednesday.

The notices caution citizens to "remain vigilant of their surroundings and practice sound personal security and situational awareness," especially at holiday-themed events.

URGENT TRAVEL ALERT AS NATIONWIDE STRIKE THREATENS WIDESPREAD DISRUPTION AND DELAYS

"U.S. citizens should exercise extra vigilance at holiday festivals and events and other locations with large crowds," it also says. 

Officials added that visitors to congested and popular tourist areas should pay particular attention to their surroundings and always follow the instructions of police and emergency response officials.

AMERICANS WARNED ABOUT PARIS TRAVEL AFTER VIOLENCE, LOOTING AND TEAR GAS-FILLED STREETS

item.title: ABC News quietly suspended staffers behind botched story on Trump sons' business dealings
item.description: ABC News quietly sidelined two staffers behind the botched Anduril report involving Donald Trump Jr., while a spokesperson says no one's employment status has changed.
item.content:encoded:
ABC News quietly suspended staffers involved in the botched story last month suggesting impropriety in the Trump sons' business dealings, Fox News Digital has confirmed.

The Disney-owned network stirred controversy with its report headlined, "Trump sons' investments have won billions in Pentagon contracts since his election," alleging that Anduril, the company investing in a new Baltimore shipyard, had ties to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump through 1789 Capital, a venture capital firm. The report claimed the firm had a "major stake" in Anduril, which was ultimately false.

ABC News raised eyebrows when it deleted the report without explanation after the story was called out on social media, then quietly republished a revised version of the report with an editor's note acknowledging the error.

GOP SENATOR CALLS FOR FCC PROBE OF ABC NEWS OVER TRUMP SONS-ANDURIL 'POLITICAL HIT JOB'

The ordeal resulted in an internal probe to determine what went wrong. While two staffers behind the botched story were reprimanded and rumors they will be terminated swirl, an ABC News spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "No one's employment status has changed." 

ABC News declined further comment. 

The Wall Street Journal's Joe Flint first reported that the two staffers were on "paid leave."

ABC News' original story wrote, "1789 Capital — a venture capital firm that lists Donald Trump Jr. as one of six partners along with three founders — claimed a major stake in Anduril in June 2025 from a $2.5 billion investment into the company."

"Since that investment, Anduril has been awarded 135 other contracts with the U.S. government and to date has received around $1.8 billion from those agreements, according to active defense contracts posted to SAM.gov, the official system for government contracting," the story continued. "The company is one of the largest manufacturers to receive an investment from Donald Trump Jr. and his brother Eric Trump, but they are not the only one."

ABC NEWS QUIETLY REPUBLISHES GUTTED VERSION OF STORY ON TRUMP SONS IT HAD DELETED WITHOUT EXPLANATION

Alexa Henning, a spokesperson for 1789 Capital and a former chief of staff to the director of national intelligence, took to social media, insisting the company does not have a "major stake" in Anduril and blasting the "biased hit piece."

"Here's a small lesson, that I also explained to ABC, the ‘reporter’ who is a complete idiot conflated raising funds with investment by 1789. Those are two separate actions," Henning reacted at the time.

"Meaning the ‘investments’ mentioned were actually the total number raised for a funding round, that MANY companies contribute to," Henning continued. "Another thing that the reporter buried the lead on was that many of these companies have gotten government contracts during Biden AND Trump, which completely negates the assertion by ABC that Don Jr and Eric Trump are doing anything wrong."

VENTURE CAPITAL FIRM TIED TO DONALD TRUMP JR WEIGHS LEGAL ACTION AGAINST ABC NEWS OVER BOTCHED REPORT

ABC News then sparked confusion among critics when it deleted the entire story, only to republish an overhauled version of the story days later with the new headline reading, "New shipyard announced amid earlier Democratic concerns about potential conflicts of interest" while stressing to readers that Trump Jr. "is not involved in investment decisions."

"CORRECTION: A version of this story published on Oct. 7 contained errors in the description of certain company investments, government contracts and event chronologies," the editor's note read at the top of the article. "After subsequent reporting, this version contains corrected information and additional context regarding some of those investments, contracts and events."

Henning has said that nobody from ABC News asked 1789 for comment prior to the initial story being published and that an ABC News journalist "vigorously defended" the report before it was suddenly deleted. She also previously said the company was considering legal action against the Disney-owned news organization. 

"This should be a cautionary tale for any other reporters who continue to traffic in this false narrative," Henning told Fox News Digital on Wednesday when asked if a lawsuit is still being considered.

item.title: Susan Smith's ex-husband wants her ‘in prison until she dies’ after killing sons in alleged bid to win lover
item.description: David Smith says he wants Susan Smith to stay in prison until she dies for killing their sons as the South Carolina parole board weighs her request.
item.content:encoded:
Susan Smith’s ex-husband wants her to remain in prison until she dies for killing their two sons in what prosecutors say was a bid to win back her lover, as a seven-member board prepares to consider her parole request Thursday.

"If I have a choice, I’d want her to stay in prison until she dies," David Smith said. "32 years hasn’t changed the heartache."

While Susan Smith was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to life in prison in 1995, state law at the time allowed her to be considered for parole after serving 30 years. item.title: Nike promises free sneakers to every high school valedictorian in America after viral request

item.content:encoded:
You don't have to be a star athlete to score free Nike sneakers. Apparently, being a straight-A student will do the trick, too.

The giveaway comes as Nike works to broaden its appeal and rebuild its brand after years of leaning into politically charged marketing campaigns. Under CEO Elliott Hill, the company has made a concerted effort to return to its roots, focusing on sports, achievement and connecting with consumers. And rewarding students for academic excellence seems like a pretty easy way to win some goodwill across the political spectrum.

item.title: Rare anti-government protests erupt in Iran over workers' deaths
item.description: Hundreds of Iranians chanted "Death to the dictator!" in Abdanan after a bus crash killed 13 oil refinery employees, with at least seven people arrested.
item.content:encoded:
Hundreds of Iranians took to the streets chanting "Death to the dictator!" and other anti-government messages in the wake of a deadly bus crash over the weekend that killed 13 employees of an oil refinery company, reports said.

The rare display of anti-government anger unfolded Tuesday in Abdanan, a city in western Iran near the country's border with Iraq. Demonstrators called for the resignation of company officials blamed for the accident.

"Those who seek to exploit this incident to disrupt public order and inflame people’s emotions will be dealt with decisively," local prosecutor Amrollah Meysaei was quoted by Iran's Mizan news agency as saying, according to Radio Free Europe.

The outlet, citing Iran's Fars news agency, also reported that an estimated 1,000 people took part in the protests, making them the largest demonstrations since mass unrest swept across Iran at the beginning of this year. Some of the protesters reportedly tried to damage public property.

IRAN LAUNCHES DRONE ASSAULT ON KUWAIT AFTER US STRIKE ON IRGC MISSILE SITE

A video verified by The Associated Press showed protesters chanting "Death to the dictator!"

A video shared by HRANA, a rights group based outside Iran, also showed a crowd of protesters marching through the center of Abdanan, calling for accountability for the road accident.

The Hengaw Organization for Human Rights said at least seven people were arrested in Abdanan after Tuesday's protests.

Two were later released, including a 15-year-old boy, Hengaw said.

LEAKED IRAN REPORT FINDS RECORD PUBLIC ANGER AS REGIME FOCUSES ON HOLDING POWER

In January, Iran witnessed some of the largest anti-government protests since the 1979 Islamic Revolution and Abdanan was a hotspot of unrest.

Security forces shot thousands of protesters in the streets and arrested thousands more during those demonstrations.

In late July, small protests broke out in the central city of Isfahan ahead of the public hanging of two protesters.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Protesters call for regime change in Iran following deadly crash that killed 13 oil and gas workers
item.description: Hundreds take to the streets in western Iran after 13 oil workers are killed, with demonstrations escalating into political protests against Tehran's leadership.
item.content:encoded:
Hundreds of protesters poured into the streets of western Iran on Tuesday following a deadly bus crash that killed 13 oil and gas workers, with demonstrations quickly escalating into anti-government chants with some protesters calling for the return of the Pahlavi monarchy.

The unrest erupted in Abdanan, a city in Iran's Ilam province near the Iraqi border, where residents initially gathered to demand accountability for Saturday's fatal accident before turning their anger toward the Islamic Republic's leadership.

Videos obtained by Fox News Digital showed large crowds marching through the streets, chanting "Death to the dictator!"

IRANIAN PROTESTER HANGED HOURS AFTER MARRYING HIS IMPRISONED FIANCÉE OVER JAIL PHONE LINE

Iranian-American journalist and foreign policy analyst Lisa Daftari said the demonstrations underscore the deeper political tensions facing Tehran. "Abdanan is a reminder that the Islamic Republic sits on top of a dormant volcano," Daftari told Fox News Digital. "These uprisings start with different catalysts, and in this case it was a local grievance, but they always arrive at the same conclusion."

"The slogans we hear are ‘Death to the Dictator’ and ‘Javid Shah,’ not complaints about a policy. They are an indictment of the entire system, top to bottom," she said.

New reports Wednesday indicated that Iranian security forces arrested at least seven people, including a 15-year-old boy, during the unrest in Abdanan.

The Hengaw Organization for Human Rights said two detainees had been released, but the whereabouts of five others remained unknown. The Kurdistan Human Rights Network separately reported that security forces fired tear gas at demonstrators and that internet access was disrupted during the crackdown.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard-affiliated Fars news agency acknowledged the demonstrations, reporting that approximately 200 to 300 people initially gathered in Abdanan's Vali-e Asr Square before the crowd grew to roughly 1,000.

Fars reported that the slogans initially focused on the deadly accident but subsequently took on a political character. Police were deployed as protesters moved into surrounding streets, according to AFP's Nov. 17 report.

ONE GLARING ISSUE GOES UNADDRESSED IN UN CHIEF'S HIGH-STAKES TALKS WITH IRAN'S PRESIDENT

The protests followed Saturday's overturning of a bus transporting workers from the Dehloran gas processing project. Thirteen people were killed and more than a dozen injured, according to Iranian media reports.

Euronews Persian reported on Nov. 17 that provincial traffic police identified driver negligence, irregularities involving the company's bus contract and inadequate road barriers as factors contributing to the accident. Prosecutors have announced legal proceedings against the company and provincial transportation officials, although responsibility has not been established in court.

Authorities warned against allowing the demonstrations to escalate.

"Individuals who seek to exploit this incident to disrupt public order or incite public sentiment will be dealt with firmly," Abdanan prosecutor Amrollah Misaie said, according to Iran's judiciary-affiliated Mizan news agency, as quoted by AFP on Nov. 17.

Daftari, The Foreign Desk editor-in-chief, argued that the Iranian government's greatest challenge may ultimately come from within, regardless of its confrontation with Washington and Jerusalem. "Whatever happens in the military standoff with the United States and Israel, Tehran will still face its most serious adversary at home," she said.

She also pointed to the protesters' willingness to return to the streets following the deadly crackdown earlier this year, saying that "despite thousands being killed by the regime for protesting in January, we still see bravery on the part of the Iranian people to tell the world of their grievances and to stand up to their murderers."

At the United Nations' daily briefing on Tuesday, Fox News Digital asked the U.N. spokesperson whether the organization was monitoring the situation, particularly the actions of Iranian security forces on the ground. "Well, we're keeping an eye on the situation and we want to make sure that all peaceful protests are allowed to proceed without obstruction and without harassment of protesters," the spokesperson said and added, "Certainly our human rights colleagues will continue to monitor the situation as we've done in the past."

IRAN TURNS CITIZENS INTO INFORMANTS AS CHILLING CRACKDOWN SPREADS BEYOND ITS BORDERS

The demonstrations carry particular significance because Abdanan was previously a flashpoint during Iran's nationwide anti-government protests earlier this year.

Reuters reported on Jan. 9 that it had verified footage showing demonstrators marching through the city during the broader uprising against the Islamic Republic.

The city also witnessed renewed tensions during mourning ceremonies for protesters killed in the January unrest. Reuters reported on Feb. 18 that witnesses and activists said security forces opened fire on hundreds of mourners gathered at a cemetery in Abdanan.

Tuesday's demonstrations mark another outbreak of public anger in a city with a recent history of confrontations with Iranian authorities.
